title: Mark Athena-Verifier trailer "none" when no verifier ran
summary: Review note n2 says a job rejected by a check before any verifier ran still gets `Athena-Verifier: <model> fail`, which reads as if the verifier model judged it. The closing commit should instead carry a trailer such as `Athena-Verifier: none (check fmt failed)`. The audience is anyone reading the job's commit trailers.

defaults_applied.how: Add unit tests for both trailer forms; cargo test and clippy must pass.
The criteria check the trailer text produced for a check-failed job, not that code exists.
One focused change to trailer construction plus its doc line.
The trailer is keyed on whether a verifier actually ran, which covers every pre-verifier rejection, not only the fmt case.
Behavior criteria name the cargo commands the verifier can run.
The docs line explains the `none` trailer for outside readers.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: In run.rs, `closing.verification` is built even when checks fail and the verifier is skipped (`verifier_invocation` stays None), and that is what produces the misleading trailer (read at lines 1032-1236 and 1432-1444).
The trailer is built at run.rs:1432-1444 using `ctx.reading.verifier_model`. The pass/fail wording is unchanged when a verifier did run.
The new value is `none (check <name> failed)`, naming the first failed check in `verification.checks` (`CheckRun.name`, `passed`). It is the review's own example.
Landed jobs always had a verifier run, so only rejected or failed closings change. The re-landing path at run.rs:1743 copies trailers verbatim and needs no change.
Prose in docs/records.md (line 121) describing the trailer gets a short note about the `none` form.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new unit test in athena-core builds the closing trailers for a verification whose `verifier_invocation` is None and has a failed check named fmt. It asserts the `Athena-Verifier` value is `none (check fmt failed)` and does not contain the verifier model name. Run `cargo test -p athena-core`.
A test asserts that when a verifier ran, the trailer is still `<verifier-model> pass` or `<verifier-model> fail`. Run `cargo test`.
`cargo test` passes, `cargo clippy` is clean, and `cargo fmt --check` passes.
In crates/athena-core/src/run.rs, the Athena-Verifier trailer is chosen by whether a verifier invocation exists, not only by the final verdict. The model name appears only when a verifier ran.
docs/records.md describes the `Athena-Verifier: none (check <name> failed)` form beside the existing `<model> pass` line. A reader of a rejected job's commit can tell that no verifier judged it.
The change is focused: no governance files change, and CHANGELOG.md gets one entry only if the repo's convention requires it.

out_of_scope: n1 and n3 and the other review findings
Changing what the verifier is told about its snapshot
Changing verdict, outcome, or scoring logic
departures: Slightly higher pass probability and lower cost than the reference: the change is small and local, with a clear fix stated in the review.
